migration.description: Bind Connector-issued Hosts and credentials to the durable device authorization so retries reuse one enrollment result.
migration.release_unit_description: Phase-one Connector exchange retry hardening after migration 00019.

compatibility_assessment.reason: The migration adds nullable foreign-key bindings used only by Connector device enrollment retries; existing Host registrations and credentials remain unchanged.

durable_state.description: A device authorization may identify at most one Host registration and one Host credential. The foreign keys are nullable and clear when expired device rows are removed.
durable_state.storage_implementation: PostgreSQL columns and partial unique indexes managed by the embedded Goose application migration history.

source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Phase-one Connector enrollment idempotency candidate containing migration 00020.
source_compatibility_range.compatibility_boundary: Older candidates ignore the additive nullable columns. New Connector exchanges use the binding; legacy Host registration and enrollment paths leave it NULL.

ordered_operations.description: Add a nullable device-authorization foreign key and partial unique index to Host registrations.
Add the corresponding nullable device-authorization foreign key and partial unique index to Host credentials.

database_migration.backfill: none; only new Connector exchanges write the binding.
rollout_signals: One authorization record resolves to one Host and credential under concurrent retry.
Retry derives the same opaque token from the authorization code and durable Host/credential identities without storing the raw code or token.

recovery.faulty_release_recovery: forward-repair-by-a-new-program-version-or-compatible switchback while nullable bindings remain readable

validation: Fresh and upgraded PostgreSQL databases apply migration 00020 with all partial unique indexes present.
Concurrent and stale device exchange retries reuse one Host/credential result.
Legacy Host registrations and credentials remain valid with NULL Connector bindings.
